newsitem.title: UK: YTV in takeover talks with Granada.
newsitem.headline: YTV in takeover talks with Granada.

text.p: Yorkshire-Tyne Tees Television Holdings Plc confirmed on Monday it is in talks with Granada Group Plc about an offer by Granada for the shares in YTV it does not already own.
The offer would value Yorkshire shares at 1.175 pounds ($1.91) per share. Yorkshire's shares had closed 57-1/2 pence higher at 1.165 pounds on Monday.
YTV in takeover talks with Granada =2

Any offer would require the prior approval of Britain's Takeover Panel and its completion would be conditional on the consent of the Independent Television Commission, the companies said in a joint statement.
Granada, the hotel-to-leisure group, had built up a 27 percent stake in Yorkshire TV and has long been expected to mount a takeover bid.
Speculation intensified following a report in this week's Sunday Times saying that Granada was close to negotiating a takeover.
The newspaper said talks between the two companies had resumed after Granada chairman Gerry Robinson and chief executive Charles Allen attended Yorkshire's annual meeting four weeks ago.
A Yorkshire TV spokesman said on Sunday in response to the Sunday Times report that timing and pricing would be the key to a successful takeover bid by Granada.
Based on the current issued equity of 55.23 million shares, a 11.75 pounds per share offer would value YTV at around 650 million pounds. ($ = 0.612 British Pounds)
